summary.intent: Complete the ship phase for Phase 69 on the cipher-box repo: open PR #594 with ship-review fixes applied, then get it through CI, Desktop E2E, and CodeRabbit/Greptile review triage to a mergeable green state.
summary.outcome: PR #594 opened and pushed with 10 verified ship-review fixes (incl. a CRITICAL read-after-write EIO regression); 6 Greptile review threads triaged (4 already-covered, 1 intentional flag-day cutover, 1 anti-rollback finding sent for expert verification); cargo-windows and Windows Desktop E2E failures were root-caused to the pre-existing, unexecuted plan 69-14 (WinFsp migration) rather than the ship-review changes, and the user's concurrent push of 69-14 merged cleanly on top without clobbering prior work.

repo: In cipher-box's generation-gating design, `fetch_node_gated` deliberately passes the *expected* generation (parent's SealedChildRef mirror, or stored floor for own-resolve) — never the fetched node's own envelope generation — mirroring the TS `dfsFindFolder` rule; a floor-vs-floor comparison on own-resolve looks like a no-op but is offset by IPNS record signing + seq gating.

vault.rs intentionally fail-closed rejects v2-format blobs (comment at lines 357-358) as part of a clean pre-launch flag-day cutover — not a backward-compat bug, same disposition as the previously-deferred bin.rs legacy-decode finding.

Plan 69-14 (WinFsp Windows platform-layer migration) is marked `autonomous:false`/D-06 because winfsp can't compile on macOS, so it's expected to be done by the user on their own Windows box and was the true cause of cargo-windows failing with 47 compile errors, all confined to `crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/*`.

The macOS Desktop E2E flake pattern: build/infra succeeds, uploads/publishes/mkdir succeed for ~5 min, then exit code 4/'Terminated: 15' — a timeout kill, not an assertion failure; recurring 'queue: malformed entry ... skipped' warnings are expected-handled noise, not panics.

code.finding: Greptile P1: self-resolve path compares floor-vs-floor for the generation gate (a no-op in isolation) — flagged for expert security review since IPNS signing/seq gating may offset it; see high_water.rs enforce_resolved and listing.rs comment lines 14-17 for the documented design rationale.
Fail-closed rejection of v2 vault blobs is intentional per comment at lines 357-358 (clean flag-day cutover, no prod v2 vaults expected) — not a backward-compat regression.

All 47 cargo-windows compile errors originate here from stale pre-node/v3 call signatures (e.g. `fetch_and_decrypt_content_async` legacy args, `cid: String` vs `str`); referenced 'function defined here' notes at content_ops.rs:133, events.rs:91, journal_helpers.rs:423 are just the shared-function definitions, not the fault.

workflow: zsh treats `$status` as a read-only special variable — using it as a custom variable name in a background polling script causes a silent exit-code-1 failure; use a different variable name.

When a release bot pushes a `chore(release)` commit on top of an open PR, check-run IDs change and CodeRabbit/other reviews re-trigger against the new HEAD — factor this into review-thread triage timing.

Before concluding a CI failure is caused by your own changes, check whether it maps to a known-unexecuted/deferred plan item (e.g. grep error paths against planning docs) — confirms scope and avoids wasted debugging.

When a user pushes concurrent work to a branch you've also pushed to, verify via `git log`/divergence check that the push landed as a clean merge rather than clobbering prior commits before continuing.

friction: Background poll script failed because `$status` is a read-only zsh variable — required a rework with a differently-named variable.
cargo-windows and Windows Desktop E2E both failed, requiring root-cause analysis to distinguish pre-existing unexecuted plan gaps (69-14) from real regressions introduced by the ship-review fixes.
macOS Desktop E2E also failed independently (timeout/termination), requiring separate investigation to rule out a regression from the `read_ops` change versus the known FUSE-T flake.
Concurrent pushes (ship-review fixes, release-bot commit, and the user's 69-14 winfsp work) created a time-sensitive risk of clobbering work, requiring careful divergence checks before syncing.
open_items: Confirm listing.rs:689 anti-rollback generation-gate finding via the dispatched security-reviewer agent before closing out that Greptile thread.
